newsitem.title: UK: London murders down to 15-year low - police say.
newsitem.headline: London murders down to 15-year low - police say.

text.p: The murder rate in London has fallen to a 15-year low and its police chief said the record was the envy of New York crime-busters.
Newly-released figures showed that the number of murders in London, a city of seven million people, dropped to 144 last year from 171 in 1995.
Police chief Sir Paul Condon said detectives had been successful in tackling armed robbers, contract killers and turf wars between drug dealers.

"New York would trade our crime figures for theirs any day of the week. New York has about 1,000 murders a year, almost 10 times our rate even with their zero tolerance campaign, they would love to have our murder rates," he told reporters.
New York's "zero tolerance" campaign cracks down on petty crime to discourage more serious crime.
